title: Find a high-quality freelancer on Fiverr
description: Use a checklist of trust signals (badges, reviews, response time, red flags) to pick a freelancer on Fiverr instead of picking the cheapest result.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: What you want done (e.g. 'logo design for SaaS')

parameters.name: budget_usd
parameters.description: Budget ceiling per gig, in USD

steps.intent: Open Fiverr search for the user's query
Apply trust filters before scanning results
steps.notes: Tighten the candidate pool first — only then start judging individual sellers.
criteria: Filter by 'Top Rated Seller' or 'Pro' badge
Sort by 'Best Selling' so reviews-per-gig is high
Set delivery time to ≤ the deadline you actually need
Cap budget at the {{budget_usd}} value the user provided

steps.intent: Read each candidate's profile against trust signals
steps.notes: On the gig page, scan for signals before reading the pitch.
criteria: ≥ 100 reviews with a ≥ 4.9 average — fewer = thin evidence
Response time under 1 hour suggests an active seller
Portfolio shows the same style/category as the request
Recent reviews (last 30 days) are positive and specific

steps.intent: Watch for red flags in the seller's behavior
steps.notes: These usually mean walk away — even if the price is right.
criteria: Seller does not ask any clarifying questions in their pitch — they will deliver something generic
Reviews mention 'used a template' or 'didn't read brief'
Profile is < 6 months old with no Top Rated badge
Heavy upsell language ('contact me first for the real price')
All reviews are 5★ but suspiciously short (one-word praise)

steps.intent: Open the strongest candidate's gig page to start the order

sourceVideo.title: How to find best freelancers on Fiverr
